doc.title: Dick Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Sol Yaged, favorite listening and Bobby Hackett
summary: He mentions Sol Yaged at Donnell Library, listens to old CDs by Bobby Hackett and Wild Bill Davison, and tells a Hackett story.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: You ever run into Sol Yaged?
Yes. Sol used to come every once in a while, drop in to our concerts down at the Donnell Library.
Yeah. Who do you listen to these days?
Bobby Hackett, did I mention him? I hope so.

I love him. He’s a nice contrast. I play a little bit of him and then a little bit of Wild Bill Davison. And on the average I’m okay. It’s like the fellow who stands on one bare foot on a block of ice and the other bare foot in the fire and on the average he’s comfortable.
Yeah. Interesting. Yeah I think it was another Bill Crow story about Bobby Hackett selling one of his trumpets and he said “high register never used.”

That’s right. And somebody once said to him, and this was on a radio interview, “Bobby you’re known for never having a bad word about anybody. Praise, yes, but you’ll never criticize anybody. So what if somebody said ‘Adolph Hitler?’” So Bobby thinks a minute and he says, “Well I guess you’d have to say that he was tops in his line.”
